summary: Coverage-forced gold LoRA adapter, epoch 1, greedy
hypothesis: Distilling Sonnet's coverage-forced reasoning — where Sonnet explicitly reasons across seven decision axes before writing one atomic question per axis — into the 3B adapter weights should lift the coverage dimension that every in-context lever failed to move, because the gap is per-task judgment about which axes matter, not instructions.
technique: A single greedy on-device call using a LoRA adapter (adapter_v2b_e1) fine-tuned for one epoch on 556 training pairs whose gold questions were regenerated with a coverage-forcing prompt (Sonnet reasons over seven distinct axes then writes one atomic question per axis); same lr 5e-4 recipe as v2a.
result: Scored 0.314 on the full-30 gate (0 wins / 0 ties / 29 losses vs Sonnet), rubric atom 5 / spec 3 / cover 3 / nat 4 / nonRed 3 — well below the v2a_e1 champion (0.409); critically, coverage stayed pinned at 3, the exact dimension the coverage-forced gold was built to move. The hypothesis was falsified: distilling dimensional-coverage targets does not transfer the per-task judgment of which axes matter, and the experiment was discarded.
label: adapter_v2b_e1
